messages.body_plain:
HI, I am trying to add bootstrap values from a newick file. Some searches on the internet have turned up the following code, but the values are displayed as decimals. Is there any way to multiply the number by 100 and have it cut off at the decimal point so 0.909 would show up as 91. I am also having trouble getting the numbers to display nicely at the node (i.e., rotated along the line and not overlapping other parts of the image). Here is my code:

tg = ggtree(t, layout = "circular", size = .1)
p <- tg + geom_tippoint(aes(x=x+.003, subset=(abs(angle) >= 90), angle=angle+180), fill=Fill, color=Outline, shape=Shape, size=4, stroke = .1) + xlim(-.1, .15)
q <- p + geom_treescale(x=0.05, width=.005, color='red')
r <- q + geom_text2(aes(label=label, subset=label>.07 & !isTip), hjust=-.2)
r

and the resulting tree is attached.

Other than these minor issues, I am getting close to what we want for our final product. Thank you for putting this all together!

Kind regards,
Kirston

messages.subject: Re: bootstrap values from newick format
messages.subject_clean: bootstrap values from newick format
messages.body_plain:
You can directly convert the number in `aes`.

For example:

library(ggtree)
raxml_file <- system.file("extdata/RAxML", "RAxML_bipartitionsBranchLabels.H3", package="ggtree")
raxml <- read.raxml(raxml_file)
ggtree(raxml)+ geom_text(aes(label=bootstrap/100))

But in your case, the bootstrap value is stored in node label, which should be stored in character, I recommend you converting it outside ggtree and then using the tidy data to label the bootstrap.

d = q$data
d=d[!d$isTip,]
d$label = as.numeric(d$label)
d$label = round(d$label * 100)
d=d[d$label > 70,]

q + geom_text2(data=d, aes(label=label), hjust=-.2)

messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

Really liking ggtree - thanks for this package.

I'm trying to use geom_tiplab2.  I have a vector of colors, the same length as the number of tips, but geom_tiplab2 doesn't like that.  What is the length of the aes attributes that geom_tiplab2 needs?

Borrowing an example from another post...

require(ape)
require(ggtree)
require(ggplot2)
set.seed(1234)
fulltree <- rtree(n=50, br=NULL)
#Plot with ggtree
ggtree(fulltree, layout="circular")+geom_tiplab(color = rep("blue", 50))
# works
ggtree(fulltree, layout="circular")+geom_tiplab2()
# works
length(fulltree$tip.label)
#[1] 50
ggtree(fulltree, layout="circular")+geom_tiplab2(color = rep("blue", 50))
# Error: Aesthetics must be either length 1 or the same as the data (48): colour, hjust
ggtree(fulltree, layout="circular")+geom_tiplab2(color = rep("blue", 48))
# Error: Aesthetics must be either length 1 or the same as the data (51): colour, hjust
ggtree(fulltree, layout="circular")+geom_tiplab2(color = rep("blue", 51))
# Error: Aesthetics must be either length 1 or the same as the data (48): colour, hjust
fulltree
# Phylogenetic tree with 50 tips and 49 internal nodes.
#
# Tip labels:
#     t14, t15, t25, t9, t35, t10, ...
#
# Rooted; no branch lengths.
ggtree(fulltree, layout="circular")+geom_tiplab2(color = rep("blue", 99))
# Error: Aesthetics must be either length 1 or the same as the data (48): colour, hjust
ggtree(fulltree, layout="circular")+geom_tiplab2(color = rep("blue", 100))
# Error: Aesthetics must be either length 1 or the same as the data (48): colour, hjust

messages.subject_clean: length of aes for geom_tiplab2
messages.body_plain:
just use

ggtree(fulltree, layout="circular")+geom_tiplab2(color = 'blue')

Referring to https://groups.google.com/forum/?utm_medium=email&utm_source=footer#!topic/bioc-ggtree/o35PV3iHO-0, geom_tiplab2 is just a short cut for

geom_tiplab(aes(subset=(abs(
angle) < 90), angle=angle), ...) + geom_tiplab(aes(subset=(abs(angle) >= 90), angle=angle+180), hjust=1, ...)

it's less flexible as geom_tiplab and just pass everything to geom_tiplab. Passing a color vector is not supported, since the color vector will pass to both geom_tiplab call and they have different lengths.

If you need to pass a color vector, use goem_tiplab instead.
